history.summary: Temple complex at Vedvyas, ~15 km from Rourkela, at the Triveni sangam where the Shankh and Koel rivers meet (with the mythical Saraswati) to form the Brahmani river. Tradition holds that Maharishi Vedavyasa spent time here and wrote the Mahabharata - his dwelling cave on a small hillock is still shown to devotees. The complex has an ancient blackstone Shiva lingam as its centrepiece, plus Saraswati Kund and shrines of Radha-Krishna, Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra. One visitor source reports a 24-hour continuous kirtan running since 27/04/1990 (UNVERIFIED). Precise founding date is not documented.

name: Vedvyas Temple
town_description: Rourkela is an industrial metropolis in Sundargarh district, northwestern Odisha, known as the 'Steel City' for the Rourkela Steel Plant commissioned in the 1950s. It sits near the confluence of the Shankh and Koel rivers that form the Brahmani. Beyond industry, it has become a tourist base for Vedvyas, Hanuman Vatika and the surrounding tribal hinterland of the Chotanagpur plateau.

travel.airport: Veer Surendra Sai Airport, Jharsuguda, ~115 km (verify); Rourkela has a small regional airport with limited flights (verify)
travel.railway: Rourkela Junction; site is ~15 km from the city, ~5 km from Panposh
travel.road: Motorable road to the riverbank complex; autos and taxis from Rourkela/Panposh

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Shravan month and Maha Shivaratri are peak pilgrimage times
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as open 24 hours by one visitor source (verify)
